source.name: Rasuwagadhi border (Bhotekoshi entering Nepal)
source.note: Ice-rock avalanche from the Lirung massif in Tibet (seismic signal 08:37, re-catalogued Ms 5.2). Debris flow ~20 km in ~7 min (~180 km/h) to Gyirong Port by 08:44. Model source is the border; the surge reached the Rasuwagadhi customs complex between ~08:50 and 09:00.

seismic_signal.desc: Seismic signal of the glacial collapse (catalogued first as M4.4, later Ms 5.2)

dhm_informed.desc: DHM Flood Forecasting Division learns of the flood by phone from the Rasuwa DAO and Betrawati station staff (09:00-09:05)

community_calls.desc: Head teacher of Tribhuvan Trishuli Secondary School gets phone calls from upstream (incl. Betrawati) and evacuates ~900 students about 10 min before the flood

official_sms.desc: SMS to 679,295 people in Rasuwa, Nuwakot, Dhading, Chitwan (09:15-09:16; the PM told Parliament 09:35). Nepali only, no location or time-to-impact

downstream_forecast.desc: Forecast that the flood will reach Dhading-Galchhi and pass Mugling within hours; alerts on the Prithvi Highway and Mugling-Narayanghat road

observations.place: Syabrubesi gauge (Bhote Koshi at Shyaprubesi, DHM 446.25)
observations.src: Kathmandu Post (08:40 reading 1.62 m); ReliefWeb (station stops 08:50), via Wikipedia timeline
observations.note: first_arrival is an upper bound: the station stopped transmitting at 08:50 after a normal 08:40 reading

observations.src: Onlinekhabar technical report, via Wikipedia timeline
observations.note: station stopped transmitting at 09:20 with last reading 3.55 m; arrival taken as ~09:20

observations.src: Team research file (Mongabay, Sep 2026); Wikipedia gives '10 minutes before the flood' with no clock time
observations.note: clock time not independently verified; also implausibly equal to Betrawati upstream. Use for the story, not calibration

observations.src: Kathmandu Post (11:26 above danger); Onlinekhabar (11:43 station and Phurke bridge swept away), via Wikipedia timeline
observations.note: 11:26 is when the gauge crossed the danger level, so the true first arrival is a little earlier. Coordinates are the OSM Malekhu place node; the station itself is destroyed and not in the DHM feed
13:00 is when authorities confirmed the flood had passed Mugling, an upper bound only

observations.place: Kali Khola gauge (Trishuli River at Kali Khola, DHM 449.91)
observations.note: peak time and stage, not first arrival. Gauge stage, not height above the DEM channel

observations.place: Devghat gauge (Narayani at Devghat, DHM 450, Chitwan)
observations.src: Wikipedia timeline (13:30 4.76 m Kathmandu Post; 15:20 arrival and 16:00 peak have no inline source; 18:30 back to ~4 m Onlinekhabar)
observations.note: This is Narayani at Devghat in Chitwan, NOT Devighat near Bidur (27.86, 85.11). Below the Trishuli-Kali Gandaki confluence, so the stage includes Kali Gandaki flow. Peak stayed below the 7.3 m warning level. 15:20 arrival is weakly sourced

observations.src: Team research file; not found in Wikipedia
observations.note: 9 m in 30 min, time of day unknown. DHM 'Trishuli at Galchi' gauge uses a datum near 360 m, so its stage is not comparable

observations.src: Team research file (settlement ~8 m above riverbed, flood rose >20 m); not found in Wikipedia
observations.note: height only, no time; needs a primary source before use

destroyed_named: Rasuwagadhi customs complex and friendship bridge
Nepal Police facilities at Timure, Rasuwagadhi, Syabrubesi
damage_reported.max_reach: Floodwaters reached settlements up to 80 m above the river (Wikipedia, citing Prasai 2026)
damage_reported.secondary_lake: Aug 28: barrier lake near the Chhochen Khola / Purepu Tsangpo confluence (Tibet) overflowed; rescue halted ~3 h; Nepal side rose only ~0.6 m

sources: https://hydrology.gov.np (gauge coordinates and warning/danger levels, DHM live feed snapshot 20261017T151626Z)
